frequency_question: How often do congressional majorities successfully enact a joint resolution of disapproval to block a major executive-branch foreign nuclear or arms transfer agreement despite presidential opposition or internal friction?
membership_rule: Includes formal resolutions of disapproval introduced under the Atomic Energy Act or Arms Export Control Act that reached floor consideration. Excludes informal expressions of concern or non-binding resolutions.
provenance_note: rate of 0% from only 3 case(s); too few to establish an extreme base rate -- treat as directional
coverage_note: 3 named; universe of major high-stakes congressional disapproval votes on Middle East arms/nuclear deals is small and fully enumerated.
known_gaps: Minor non-binding disapproval motions omitted as they lack legal force under the specific statutory review framework.
skeleton: Total major statutory nuclear/arms export disapproval attempts reaching final floor votes vs. successful blocks overcoming vetoes or executive implementation.
validity_reason: The statutory framework under the Atomic Energy Act and executive-legislative dynamics regarding foreign policy powers remain structurally stable over multi-decade horizons.
